title: SQL Data Modification Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on changing rows safely in SQL: multi-row INSERT, UPDATE with joins, DELETE vs TRUNCATE, RETURNING, upserts with ON CONFLICT and MERGE, and WHERE-guarded safe updates.

chapters.title: Data Modification Mental Model
points: DML statements (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) change rows; each runs as one atomic statement and is rolled back whole if any row fails
Every write targets a table, picks rows (WHERE or SELECT source), then sets values; no WHERE means every row is picked
Writes inside a transaction stay invisible to others until COMMIT; ROLLBACK undoes them, so BEGIN first when unsure
Constraints (PK, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, FK, CHECK) are validated per row and abort the statement on violation
Workflow habit: SELECT with the same WHERE first, check the row count, then run the write

chapters.title: INSERT with Multiple Rows and SELECT
points: Multi-row: INSERT INTO t (a,b) VALUES (1,'x'),(2,'y'),(3,'z'); one statement, one round trip, far faster than 3 separate inserts
Always list the column names; relying on table column order breaks when a column is added
INSERT ... SELECT copies rows: INSERT INTO archive (id,total) SELECT id,total FROM orders WHERE created < '2025-01-01'
Column count and types in the SELECT must match the column list; omitted columns get their DEFAULT or NULL
Multi-row VALUES is all-or-nothing: one bad row fails the whole statement

chapters.title: UPDATE with Joins and Safe Updates
points: PostgreSQL: UPDATE o SET status = c.tier FROM customers c WHERE o.customer_id = c.id
MySQL: UPDATE orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id SET o.status = c.tier WHERE c.active = 1
SQL Server: UPDATE o SET o.status = c.tier FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id
Missing the join condition in the PostgreSQL FROM form creates a cross join and rewrites every row with an arbitrary match
UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE hits every row: preview with SELECT, wrap in BEGIN, check the affected-row count, then COMMIT (MySQL: SET sql_safe_updates=1 blocks WHERE-less writes)

chapters.title: DELETE vs TRUNCATE and RETURNING
points: DELETE FROM t WHERE ... removes chosen rows, logs each row, fires row triggers, and can be rolled back

TRUNCATE TABLE t removes all rows at once with no WHERE; it is fast, resets identity or sequence counters (MySQL always, PostgreSQL only with RESTART IDENTITY), and is blocked when foreign keys reference the table
TRUNCATE is DDL in MySQL and Oracle (implicit commit, no rollback); in PostgreSQL and SQL Server it is transactional
DROP removes the table itself; DELETE and TRUNCATE keep the structure
RETURNING (PostgreSQL, SQLite, MariaDB; SQL Server uses OUTPUT) gives back affected rows: INSERT ... RETURNING id; UPDATE ... RETURNING *; DELETE ... RETURNING *

chapters.title: Upsert with ON CONFLICT and MERGE
points: PostgreSQL: INSERT INTO t (id,qty) VALUES (1,5) ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET qty = EXCLUDED.qty; EXCLUDED holds the row you tried to insert
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING skips duplicates silently; the conflict target needs a UNIQUE or PK index on those columns
MySQL equivalent: INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE qty = VALUES(qty); SQLite uses ON CONFLICT like PostgreSQL
MERGE INTO t USING src ON t.id = src.id WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET ... WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (...) VALUES (...); standard SQL in SQL Server, Oracle and PostgreSQL 15+

Pitfalls: MERGE with duplicate source keys errors or is non-deterministic, SQL Server MERGE needs a trailing semicolon and has known concurrency bugs (use HOLDLOCK), and a multi-row upsert cannot touch the same key twice

chapters.title: Data Modification Cheat Sheet
points: Insert many: INSERT INTO t (cols) VALUES (...),(...); copy: INSERT INTO t (cols) SELECT ...
Update from another table: PostgreSQL FROM, MySQL JOIN ... SET, SQL Server FROM ... JOIN
Remove rows: DELETE ... WHERE (logged, rollbackable); empty table fast: TRUNCATE; remove table: DROP
Get rows back: RETURNING (PostgreSQL) or OUTPUT (SQL Server); upsert: ON CONFLICT, ON DUPLICATE KEY, MERGE
Safe routine: SELECT preview, BEGIN, run write, check row count, COMMIT or ROLLBACK
